extra_misconceptions.fact: Dodging between parked vehicles hides you from approaching drivers and forces unpredictable merges back into moving traffic.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Weaving in and out between parked cars along the curb keeps a cyclist safer by staying out of the main traffic lane.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Keep the helmet in place if a head or neck injury is suspected so the cervical spine stays aligned until medical help arrives.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Removing a bicycle helmet immediately after a high-speed crash helps a dizzy rider breathe easier and cool down faster.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Shallow angles trap narrow bicycle tires in tracks or grates, so riders must adjust their line to cross at a ninety-degree angle.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Crossing wet railroad tracks or steel bridge grates at a shallow diagonal angle gives the tires a smoother transition.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Thirst lags behind actual fluid loss, so cyclists must sip water and replace electrolytes steadily before dehydration begins.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Drinking large amounts of plain water only after thirst sets in is enough to prevent heat exhaustion on hot rides.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a rider's front wheel when crossing railroad tracks or metal grates at a shallow angle instead of ninety degrees?
Which physical indicator distinguishes life-threatening heatstroke from heat exhaustion during a long summer cycling trip?
Where should a cyclist position their bike relative to parked cars to avoid the hazard of a driver suddenly opening a door?
Why is it dangerous to scrub deep gravel out of road rash with dry gauze before irrigating the wound with clean running water?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Bicycles must travel in the same direction as traffic because riding against traffic increases collision speed and surprises turning drivers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Riding on the left side of the road facing oncoming cars is safer because a cyclist can watch approaching vehicles.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Unless a state has a specific yield law, cyclists have the same legal duty as drivers to come to a complete stop at stop signs.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cyclists may legally roll through four-way stop signs without stopping whenever no motor vehicles are in the intersection.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Going straight from a right-turn-only lane invites a right-hook collision; move into the leftmost part of the through lane instead.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hugging the far-right curb in a dedicated right-turn-only lane is the safest position when riding straight through an intersection.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Hand signals must be given well before turning or changing lanes after scanning behind to confirm a clear gap in traffic.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Extending a hand turn signal right as you begin to swerve into the adjacent lane gives drivers behind you adequate warning.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should a cyclist position their bicycle when riding through an intersection in a lane that is too narrow to share safely?
Under what road or traffic conditions do most state laws allow a cyclist to move left from the right edge of the roadway?
What is the difference between executing a vehicular-style left turn and a pedestrian-style two-stage box left turn?
Why is it dangerous to proceed through a green light on the right side of a car or truck that has not signaled a turn?

extra_misconceptions.fact: A helmet tilted back leaves the frontal bone unprotected and must sit level just one to two finger-widths above the eyebrows.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Tilting a bicycle helmet back on the head to expose the forehead still protects the skull during a forward fall.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Impact crushes the internal foam liner permanently on the first hit, so any crashed helmet must be replaced immediately.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A bicycle helmet that survived a hard crash onto pavement remains safe to wear if the plastic outer shell has no visible cracks.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Passive reflectors only shine when hit by car beams, so night riders need an active white front light and red rear light and reflector.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Reflective clothing patches alone satisfy nighttime visibility rules without mounting an active front headlight on the bicycle.

extra_misconceptions.fact: An oversized helmet shifts during a crash, so the shell and retention dial must fit the rider's head snugly right now.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Buying an oversized helmet for a growing youth is safe if the chin strap is pulled tight underneath the jaw.

extra_socratic_questions: What measurement in finger-widths above the eyebrows confirms that a bicycle helmet sits level at the proper forehead height?
Which certification sticker inside a bicycle helmet verifies that it meets mandatory United States impact safety standards?
What happens to a helmet's expanded polystyrene foam liner after a single hard impact even when the outer shell looks undamaged?
Why do the Scouting America Bike Safety Guidelines require both a white front headlight and a red rear reflector or taillight at dusk?

extra_misconceptions.fact: A saddle that low strains the knees; proper height leaves a slight twenty-five to thirty degree knee bend at the bottom of the stroke.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Setting the saddle height so both feet rest flat on the ground while seated gives the best pedaling leverage and knee safety.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A quick-release cam must be closed by flipping the lever over center with firm palm pressure, never by twisting it like a nut.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Spinning a quick-release lever clockwise like a wingnut until it feels snug secures a bicycle wheel safely in the dropouts.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Thumb checks cannot measure pressure accurately, so always read the PSI range molded on the tire sidewall and use a pressure gauge.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Inflating every bicycle tire until it feels hard to a thumb squeeze matches the manufacturer's recommended pressure rating.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Heavy oil attracts abrasive grit, and any lubricant on brake rims or rotors destroys stopping friction; use bike lube on a clean chain.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Spraying heavy grease or motor oil onto a dirty bicycle chain and brake rims keeps the drivetrain running smoothly.

extra_socratic_questions: What knee angle at the bottom of the pedal stroke indicates that a bicycle saddle is adjusted to the proper riding height?
Which components are inspected in sequence during an ABC Quick Check before a group ride leaves the trailhead?
Why is it dangerous to align rim brake pads so that the rubber shoes rub against the tire sidewall or hang below the rim?
What happens to shifting accuracy between rear cogs when the derailleur cable has too much slack or too much tension?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Forward weight transfer gives the front wheel most of the stopping power; squeeze both brakes smoothly while shifting weight back.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Using only the rear brake during an emergency stop stops a bicycle in the shortest distance because the front brake flips you.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Derailleurs require the chain to be moving forward under light pedaling tension so the links can climb smoothly onto the next cog.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Shifting derailleur gears while the bicycle is stationary or while standing hard on the pedals helps the chain move faster.

extra_misconceptions.fact: An inside pedal at the bottom of the stroke can strike the pavement and lift the rear tire; keep the inside pedal at twelve o'clock.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pushing the inside pedal all the way down to the bottom of the stroke during a sharp turn lowers the center of gravity safely.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Twisting both shoulders pulls the handlebars into traffic; relax the left arm or drop the inside hand slightly while glancing back.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Turning your whole upper body and both shoulders when scanning behind for cars keeps the handlebars pointed straight ahead.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to stopping distance and rider stability if a cyclist grabs only the front brake while leaning forward?
Where should the inside pedal be positioned when leaning a bicycle through a sharp corner at moderate speed?
Why must a rider ease off pedal pressure slightly while continuing to spin the cranks during a derailleur gear shift?
Which technique allows a cyclist to scan over the left shoulder for traffic without swerving into the travel lane?

extra_misconceptions.fact: The Scouting America buddy system requires buddies to stay within sight and earshot so no rider is left alone during a mechanical failure.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Faster cyclists in a patrol should ride ahead at their own pace and wait for slower buddies only at the final destination.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Patrols must ride single file on roads with motor traffic and leave enough space between riders for passing cars to re-enter safely.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Riding two or three abreast across a narrow two-lane road is allowed on long tours so buddies can converse easily.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Standard trail etiquette requires bicyclists to yield to both hikers and equestrians, slowing down and announcing their presence early.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Bicyclists have the right of way over hikers and horses on narrow dirt trails because bicycles cannot stop as quickly.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Endurance rides require scheduled rest stops every hour to take in carbohydrates, electrolytes, and water before glycogen is depleted.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Completing a fifty-mile ride requires skipping rest stops and eating one large meal only after the tour finishes.

extra_socratic_questions: What route details and checkpoints must be recorded in a written ride plan and log for the fifty-mile cycling trip?
Under what condition does a group riding single file need to increase following distance between bicycles from two bike lengths?
Which right-of-way triangle governs yielding on shared multi-use trails when cyclists encounter hikers and equestrians?
What happens to group safety if faster riders drop a slower buddy on a climb instead of regrouping at intersections?
